VOTE RECONSIDERED - RESTORED TO THIRD READING

items.lawCode: Add Art 27 Title 18 §§27-1801 - 27-1811, En Con L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S3593

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the environmental conservation law, in relation to
recycling rechargeable batteries


 PURPOSE :
To require New York State residents to recycle rechargeable batteries
instead of disposing of them as solid waste. This law requires
rechargeable battery manufacturers to work in partnership with New
York retailers to set up a free, easily accessible recycling network
for residents.

New York retailers that sell rechargeable batteries (or products
containing rechargeable batteries) to collect rechargeable batteries
for recycling from consumers. Retailers are required to post and
maintain, at or near the point of entry to the place of business, a
legible sign stating that used rechargeable batteries of the size and
shape sold or offered by the retailer may not enter the solid waste
stream, and that the retail establishment is a collection site for
recycling such batteries at no-cost to the consumer. Retailers are
required to conspicuously maintain a collection box or other suitable
receptacle easily accessible by customers, into which consumers may
deposit used rechargeable batteries.  Online, mail, and telephone
retailers must provide this information at the time of purchase or
upon delivery of the product. Retailers must then work with the
Rechargeable Battery Recycling Corporation and their call2recycle
program, to properly recycle and/or dispose of batteries that have
been collected.

Examples of products containing rechargeable batteries include:
cellular and cordless phones, digital cameras, MP3 players, laptop
computers, remote control toys, electric razors, and cordless power
tools.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
Section 1
- Creates a new section 27-1703 of the ECL on Rechargeable batteries.

Section 2
- Prohibits the disposal of rechargeable batteries in mixed solid
waste
- Definitions

- Retailers and distributors shall accept rechargeable batteries from
any individual at no charge

- Retailers must conspicuously post a sign which states, "It is
illegal to discard rechargeable batteries, state law requires us to
accept rechargeable batteries at no charge for recycling.

- Exemptions
- Any local law or ordinance which is inconsistent with this title
shall be preempted.
- Severability clause

Section 3
- Enforcement provisions

Section 4
- Effective date

 JUSTIFICATION :


Although rechargeable batteries can reduce waste and energy because of
a longer life span than non-rechargeable batteries, they also can
contain toxic metals, such as cadmium, lead, and mercury.

Rechargeable batteries when not properly disposed of, can pollute
lakes and streams as the metals vaporize into the air when burned or
incinerated; contribute to metals leaching from solid waste landfills;
expose the environment and water supply to lead and acid
contamination; and contain strong corrosive acids; cause burns or
other damage to eyes and skin.

Members of the battery industry voluntarily started the Rechargeable
Battery Recycling Corporation (RBRC) in 1994 to encourage consumers
and retailers to participate in recycling rechargeable batteries.
However, the goals of the RBRC have fallen short. In 1998, they
forecast recycling 16.9 million pounds by 2004 in the u.s. but were
more than 70 percent short of meeting this goal collecting only 4.4
million pounds in the u.S. and Canada combined.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
Undetermined.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the first of January next succeeding the
date on which it shall have become a law.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S3593A

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the environmental conservation law, in relation to
recycling rechargeable batteries


 PURPOSE :

To require New York State residents to recycle rechargeable batteries
instead of disposing of them as solid waste. This law requires
rechargeable battery manufacturers to work in partnership with New
York retailers to set up a free, easily accessible recycling network
for residents.

New York retailers that sell rechargeable batteries shall collect them
from consumers for recycling. Retailers are required to post place a
legible sign stating that used rechargeable batteries of the size and
shape sold or offered by the retailer may not enter the solid waste
stream, and that the retail establishment is a collection site for
recycling such batteries at no-cost to the consumer. Retailers are
required to conspicuously maintain a collection box or other suitable
receptacle easily accessible by customers, into which consumers may
deposit used rechargeable batteries. Online, mail, and telephone
retailers must provide this information at the time of purchase or
upon delivery of the product. Battery manufactures must then arrange
for the return and recycling of all used rechargeable batteries
collected by retailers at the manufacturer's expense.

Examples of products containing rechargeable batteries include:
cellular and cordless phones, digital cameras, MP3 players, laptop
computers, remote control toys, electric razors, and cordless power
tools.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1.

- Legislative intent and findings

Section 2.

- Creates a new section of the Environmental Conservation Law on
rechargeable battery recycling.

- Prohibits the disposal of rechargeable batteries in mixed solid
waste and requires manufacturers of rechargeable batteries to take
back and recycle the used rechargeable batteries sold or disposed of
in the state.

- Definitions Battery manufacturer, consumer, place of business,
rechargeable battery, retailer, food store,

- Rechargeable battery recycling program No person shall knowingly
dispose of rechargeable batteries as solid waste at any time in the
state.

- Rechargeable batteries shall be returned to a retailer that sells
such batteries that are similar in shape, size and function.
Batteries must be removed from the electronic product in which they
are contained.

- Retailers shall conspicuously post a legible sign stating "It is
illegal to dispose of rechargeable batteries in the state of New York

as solid waste. We accept used rechargeable batteries for return to
the manufacturer."

- Retailers that sell rechargeable batteries to consumers in the state
by catalog or mail, telephone or the internet shall provide notice of
the ability to return used rechargeable batteries at no cost to the
consumer for recycling.

- Every battery manufacturer shall arrange for the return and
recycling of all used rechargeable batteries collected by retailers,
at the manufacturer's expense.

- Within six months the effective date of this title, the battery
manufacturers will submit a plan to the commissioner to identify the
methods by which the manufacturers will collect, transport and recycle
rechargeable batteries collected by the retailers. The commissioner
must approve the plan.

- The Commissioner shall promulgate any rules and regulations needed
to implement this title

- Any person, retailer or manufacturer who violates the provisions of
this title shall be liable for civil penalties.

Section 3

- Effective date Any local law or ordinance which is inconsistent with
this title shall be preempted.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Although rechargeable batteries can reduce waste and energy because of
a longer life span than non-rechargeable batteries, they also can
contain toxic metals, such as cadmium, lead, and mercury.

Rechargeable batteries when not properly disposed of can pollute lakes
and streams as the metals vaporize into the air when burned or
incinerated; contribute to metals leaching from solid waste landfills;
expose the environment and water supply to lead and acid
contamination; and contain strong corrosive acids; cause bums or other
damage to eyes and skin.

Members of the battery industry voluntarily started the Rechargeable
Battery Recycling Corporation (RBRC) in 1994 to encourage consumers
and retailers to participate in recycling rechargeable batteries.
This bill would continue the work of the Corporation in promoting the
recycling of rechargeable batteries.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect one year after it shall have become a law,
except that section 271811 of the Environmental conservation law,
shall take effect eighteen months after it shall have become a law.

BILL NUMBER:  S3593C

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the environmental conservation law, in relation to
recycling rechargeable batteries


 PURPOSE :

To require New York State residents to recycle rechargeable batteries
instead of disposing of them as solid waste. This law requires
rechargeable battery manufacturers to work in partnership with New
York retailers to set up a free, easily accessible recycling network
for residents.

New York retailers that sell rechargeable batteries shall collect them
from consumers for recycling. Retailers are required to post a legible
sign stating that used rechargeable batteries of the size and shape
sold or offered by the retailer may not enter the solid waste stream,
and that the retail establishment is a collection site for recycling
such batteries at no-cost to the consumer. Retailers are required to
conspicuously maintain a collection box or other suitable receptacle
easily accessible by customers, into which consumers may deposit used
rechargeable batteries. Online, mail, and telephone retailers must
provide this information at the time of purchase or upon delivery of
the product. Battery manufactures must then arrange for the return and
recycling of all used rechargeable batteries collected by retailers at
the manufacturer's expense.

Examples of products containing rechargeable batteries include:
cellular and cordless phones, digital cameras, MP3 players, laptop
computers, remote control toys, electric razors, and cordless power
tools.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1.

- Legislative intent and findings

Section 2.

- Creates a new section of the Environmental Conservation Law on
rechargeable battery recycling

- Prohibits the disposal of rechargeable batteries in mixed solid
waste and requires manufacturers of rechargeable batteries to take
back and recycle the used rechargeable batteries sold or disposed of
in the state.

- Definitions
Battery manufacturer, consumer, place of business, rechargeable
battery, retailer, food store,

- Rechargeable battery recycling program
No person shall knowingly dispose of rechargeable batteries as solid
waste at any time in the state.

- Rechargeable batteries shall be returned to a retailer that sells
such batteries that are similar in shape, size and function.
Batteries must be removed from the electronic product in which they
are contained.

- Retailers shall conspicuously post a legible sign stating "It is

- Retailers that sell rechargeable batteries to consumers in the state

the ability to return used rechargeable batteries at no cost to the

- Every battery manufacturer shall arrange for the return and
recycling of all used rechargeable batteries collected by retailers,
at the manufacturer's expense.

- Within six months the effective date of this title, the battery

methods by which the manufacturers will collect, transport and recycle
rechargeable batteries collected by the retailers. The commissioner
must approve the plan.

- The Commissioner shall promulgate any rules and regulations needed
to implement this title.

- Any person, retailer or manufacturer who violates the provisions of
this title shall be liable for civil penalties.

- State Preemption

Jurisdiction in all matters pertaining to rechargeable battery
recycling is, by this title, vested exclusively in the state. Any
provision of any local law or ordinance, or any rule or regulation
promulgated thereto, governing rechargeable battery recycling shall,
upon the effective date of section 27-1805 of this title, be
preempted; provided, however, that nothing in this section shall
preclude a person from coordinating, for recycling or reuse, the
collection of rechargeable batteries.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Although rechargeable batteries can reduce waste and energy because of
a longer life span than non-rechargeable batteries, they also can
contain toxic metals, such as cadmium and lead.

Rechargeable batteries when not properly disposed of can pollute lakes
and streams as the metals vaporize into the air when burned or
incinerated; contribute to metals leaching from solid waste landfills;
expose the environment and water supply to lead and acid
contamination; and contain strong corrosive acids; cause bums or other
damage to eyes and skin.

Members of the battery industry voluntarily started the Rechargeable
Battery Recycling Corporation (RBRC) in 1994 to encourage consumers
and retailers to participate in recycling rechargeable batteries.
This bill would continue the work of the Corporation in promoting the
recycling of rechargeable batteries.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately; provided, however that section
27-1805 of the environmental conservation law, as added by section two
of this act, shall take effect on the three hundred sixtieth day after
it shall have become a law.

summary: Provides for the recycling of rechargeable batteries and prohibits disposal as solid waste, includes definitions and civil sanctions.
